learning_outcomes.text: Know the basics of the design of logical networks and the fundamental elements of the architecture of a digital computer.
Learn the basics of assembly programming languages.
Understand binary representation of information, logic circuits, and computer architecture.
Use binary representation and boolean logic.
Analyze and synthesize simple logic circuits, both combinational and sequential ones.
Ability to recognize and evaluate computer's features and performance.
Ability to find the best solution to a given problem.
The student should present and revise his knowledge, with a particular focus on the lexicon and technical jargon.
Students will learn a very low-level language, far to their usual abstraction level and intuitive developing schema. Moreover, they have to delve into collateral aspects of the discussed arguments.

syllabus_topics: Boolean Algebra. Boolean expression and function. Theorems
Combinatory Logic circuits synthesis. Truth Tables. Canonical Forms.
Decoder, multiplexer, Half and Full Adder, ALU
SR Bistable, latch SR and D, FlipFlops SR, D, JK and T
Finite State Machines, Mealy and Moore models, state diagram
Main registers: ACC, IR, MDR and MAR.
Hardwired and micro programmed Control Unit
Functions: stack frame, SP and BP.
Cache memory. Spatial and temporal locality
Memory mapped I/O and isolated I/O

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory test (eligibility for the oral exam)

assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a laboratory test for eligibility and an oral exam that determines the final score. Both tests are conducted at the end of the course. The laboratory test involves developing an IA32 assembly function that interfaces with a C main program using the OLJAsm platform. The oral exam has about 3 questions concerning the theory of computers, with 10 points per question. No material is allowed during the oral exam.
